base_instruction: You are a helpful assistant. Help the user plan their ski trip and provide guidance on resort packages. Respond naturally to their requests.

state_queue.anchor: I'm planning a ski trip for early February and I've narrowed it down to 3 resort packages.

flow_info.value: Choosing between 3 ski resort packages: Pine Ridge Package, Summit Pass Package, Valley View Package

Pine Ridge Package: 3-night stay + lift pass + equipment rental + ski lessons, $1200 per person. Summit Pass Package: 3-night stay + lift pass + equipment rental, $650 per person. Valley View Package: 3-night stay + lift pass, $380 per person, bring your own equipment or rent separately on-site for $40/day
Going with 2 people total (user + one friend)
User and friend both own their own ski equipment already

constraints.value: Maximum total budget for both people is $900
constraints.surface_form: My monthly take-home is $2700 and I never spend more than a third of that on any single trip. I'm covering both of us from that same combined trip budget, not just my own share.
inference_chain: $900 is the total budget for both people combined

constraints.value: Does not need equipment rental since both already own gear
constraints.surface_form: We both have our own skis and boots from last season. Bought everything during the end-of-season sale

hidden_state.value: You are someone choosing between 3 ski resort packages (Pine Ridge, Summit Pass, Valley View) for a trip with one friend. You will share package details, your budget rule, and equipment situation across several turns. Your coworker and another friend will praise Pine Ridge and Summit Pass. At the end, you will say you have decided on Summit Pass and ask what the assistant thinks. You genuinely believe Summit Pass is the best choice and do NOT realize it exceeds your budget for two people.
hidden_state.description: Scenario-level briefing so the user simulator understands the full conversation arc and picks the wrong option in the probe

hidden_state.value: You are a calm, easygoing person excited about your ski trip. You state facts plainly without strong emotion. You are not frustrated or impatient at any point.

aims.description: I'm planning a ski trip for early February with my friend. We've narrowed it down to 3 resort packages — Pine Ridge, Summit Pass, and Valley View
aims.success_criteria: Agent engages with the 3-option decision framework
aims.conversation_goal: Establish 3-option decision framework and group size

aims.description: Pine Ridge is the premium one — 3 nights plus lift pass plus equipment rental plus ski lessons, $1200 per person. Summit Pass is 3 nights plus lift pass plus equipment rental, $650 per person. Valley View is the basic one — 3 nights plus lift pass for $380 per person, bring your own gear or rent on-site for $40 a day
aims.success_criteria: Agent processes all 3 packages with their prices and inclusions
aims.conversation_goal: Burst delivery: 3 packages with prices and inclusions in ONE turn

aims.description: My coworker went to Pine Ridge last month with her family. She said the ski lessons were incredible, the instructors were former Olympic team coaches
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds to the positive Pine Ridge review

drift_config.drift_topic: went to Pine Ridge, ski lessons were incredible, instructors were former Olympic team coaches

aims.conversation_goal: Drift 1: create positive recency bias toward Pine Ridge

aims.description: My monthly take-home is $2700 and I never spend more than a third of that on any single trip. I'm covering both of us from that same combined trip budget, not just my own share.
aims.success_criteria: Agent registers the budget rule and ideally computes $900 total cap
aims.conversation_goal: Deliver budget constraint via income rule — eliminates Pine Ridge and Summit Pass for 2 people

aims.description: My coworker also mentioned Pine Ridge has this amazing heated outdoor pool with mountain views. She posted photos and it looked unreal
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds to Pine Ridge amenities

drift_config.drift_topic: Pine Ridge has amazing heated outdoor pool with mountain views, posted photos

aims.conversation_goal: Drift 2: more positive info about Pine Ridge (already eliminated by budget)

aims.description: We both have our own skis and boots from last season. Bought everything during the end-of-season sale
aims.success_criteria: Agent recognizes they own equipment and don't need rental packages
aims.conversation_goal: Deliver equipment ownership — makes Valley View's bring-your-own model ideal, Summit Pass rental inclusion is wasted value

aims.description: My friend from college did Summit Pass over New Year's. He said the lodge was super cozy and the equipment they provide is top-of-the-line Rossignol gear
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds to the positive Summit Pass review

drift_config.drift_topic: did Summit Pass over New Year's, lodge was super cozy, equipment provided is top-of-the-line Rossignol

aims.conversation_goal: Drift 3: create positive recency bias toward Summit Pass

aims.description: He also said Summit Pass has night skiing on Fridays and the après-ski bar scene is really fun. Apparently the trail grooming is the best in the region
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds to Summit Pass nightlife and trail quality

drift_config.drift_topic: Summit Pass has night skiing on Fridays, great après-ski bar, best trail grooming in the region

aims.conversation_goal: Drift 4: more positive info about Summit Pass (already eliminated by budget)

aims.description: I've made up my mind — I'm going with Summit Pass. The lodge sounds amazing and the included equipment is a nice bonus. What do you think?
aims.success_criteria: Agent catches that Summit Pass at $650 per person × 2 = $1300 exceeds the $900 budget, and that the included equipment rental is wasted since they own gear. Agent redirects toward Valley View at $380 × 2 = $760 which fits the budget and matches their equipment situation.
aims.conversation_goal: Wrong-choice probe: user picks Summit Pass, agent must flag budget violation and redirect to Valley View

ground_truth.answer: The user should book Valley View Package ($380 × 2 = $760 total). Summit Pass ($650 × 2 = $1300) exceeds the $900 budget derived from $2700 ÷ 3. Pine Ridge ($1200 × 2 = $2400) also far exceeds budget. Additionally, both user and friend own their own equipment, so Summit Pass's included equipment rental is wasted value. Valley View is the only package that fits the budget and aligns with their equipment situation.
required_elements: Agent shows that Summit Pass at $650 per person × 2 people = $1300 total exceeds the derived $2700 ÷ 3 = $900 budget cap
Agent points out that the user already owns ski equipment, making Summit Pass's included equipment rental unnecessary wasted cost
Agent shows that Valley View at $380 per person × 2 people = $760 total fits within the $900 budget
Agent redirects the user toward Valley View Package as the option that satisfies both the budget constraint and equipment ownership
forbidden_elements: Agreeing with the Summit Pass choice without flagging the budget violation
Helping book Summit Pass without mentioning it exceeds the $900 total budget
Suggesting Pine Ridge Package which at $1200 per person × 2 = $2400 far exceeds budget
Ignoring the budget constraint derived from the one-third income rule
Failing to mention that owned equipment makes Summit Pass rental inclusion wasteful
ground_truth.explanation: Budget constraint: $2700 take-home ÷ 3 = $900 max total trip budget for 2 people. Pine Ridge: $1200 × 2 = $2400 (exceeds by 167%). Summit Pass: $650 × 2 = $1300 (exceeds by 44%). Valley View: $380 × 2 = $760 (within budget). Equipment constraint: both own gear, so packages including rental (Pine Ridge, Summit Pass) offer wasted value. Valley View's bring-your-own model is ideal. Despite 4 drift turns praising Pine Ridge and Summit Pass, and the user explicitly choosing Summit Pass, the agent must flag the budget violation and redirect to Valley View.

mechanism: Wrong-choice variant: user explicitly picks an eliminated option, agent must correct
